chunks: As for the one who said: Allah will do what takes its place, [this is] false,
because if it were so, it would not be obligatory upon him to establish the Imam absolutely in every condition,
and that would be a matter of choice,
as we say regarding the obligatory duties (Kifayee obligations).
And in our knowledge of specifying that and its obligation in every condition is proof of the falsity of what they said.
Indeed, it is required in both cases together that [there be] knowledge.
It is said: The disbeliever, if knowledge does not become established for him, Allah will do for him what takes its place,
so knowledge will not be obligatory upon him in every condition.
ai.seo_question: Why is the appointment of the Imam considered obligatory in all conditions according to Shia theology?
ai.summary: Al-Tusi refutes the notion that Allah provides a functional substitute for the Imam by arguing that such a view would reduce the Imamate to a conditional duty (Kifayee) rather than an absolute necessity (Dharii). He employs a logical analogy regarding the disbeliever's knowledge to demonstrate that if substitution were valid, the obligation of acquiring knowledge would also become optional, thereby undermining the certainty required for divine guidance.
